formulas.formula: Plan every paycheck, see which payday pays each bill, and track what you really spend.
Fills in from the year above (this year if blank).
Weekly, every 2 weeks, twice a month or monthly.
="Your first payday this year. Using: "&IF(N(D14)=0,"none",TEXT(Paychecks!$B$2,"mmm d, yyyy"))
Twice a month only: the day of your other payday, like 15. Blank = 15 days from the first.
What lands in your bank account each payday.
Money in your account on the 1st of your first payday's month. It carries into paycheck #1.
Counted for you. See every payday on the Paychecks tab.
To change it, select the money cells and use Format > Number.
1. In YOUR SETUP, pick how often you're paid, type your first payday and your usual paycheck.
2. Open Budget Plan. List your bills with the amount, how often they come and the due date.
3. Each bill is paid by the last payday on or before its due date. That's done for you.
4. Still on Budget Plan, type how much each paycheck gives to spending (groceries, gas...) and savings.
5. Open Paychecks: Plan Balance carries what's left from one paycheck into the next. 'Short' means
the money runs out there: save more from the paychecks before it, or lower some spending.
6. Log every paycheck and purchase on Transactions: date, category and amount, on the next empty row.
7. The month tabs show each paycheck side by side: Plan vs. Actual. Paid bills turn green.
8. Bill Calendar shows which payday pays every bill, every month.
9. Use Savings Goals, Debt Payoff, Subscriptions and Net Worth to see the bigger picture.
10. Got a refund? Log it as a negative amount in the same category.
11. The example numbers show a whole year. To start fresh, go to Transactions, select columns A to F
from row 2 down and press Delete (don't delete rows). Type over the other examples, and clear
Your year at a glance: totals, charts, top categories and highlights.
Your income, bills, spending and savings, and how often each one comes.
Every payday of the year: what each paycheck covers and what's left.
Every bill, every month, and the payday that pays it.
One list for every paycheck and purchase. Everything else reads from here.
Each month's paychecks side by side: Plan vs. Actual for every category.
Every category, every month, with totals and monthly averages.
Goals with progress bars and how many paychecks to go.
Your debts, how much you paid down and months left.
Everything you pay for regularly, and what you'd save by cancelling.
What you own minus what you owe, month by month, with a chart.
White cells: type your numbers here.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you. No typing needed.
Red: something to check (a short paycheck, over plan, a missing category).
Green: paid, on track or better than planned.
Yellow: a bill due before your first payday, so it's on paycheck #1.
Bills due right after payday are the easiest to cover. Ask companies to move due dates if a paycheck is short.
A month with an extra paycheck (3 instead of 2) is perfect for savings or paying down debt.
Pay yourself first: move savings out on payday, before you spend.
Plan yearly costs (insurance, registration) as a small amount every paycheck.
Buy with a credit card? Log each purchase in its category, and only log card payments toward an old balance as a bill.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to stress-free paydays.
Everything here updates from your Transactions and Paychecks.

Amount: per paycheck for 'Every paycheck', otherwise per bill. Each bill is paid by the last payday on or before its due date. Rename categories, but don't insert or delete rows.
Left to Plan (aim for $0 or a little more)
How Often: Every paycheck (spending, savings), Monthly, Every 3 months, Every 6 months, Yearly or One time. Due Date: type a date like 1/15. For monthly bills only the day counts.
Red category name: it's listed twice, has amounts but no name, or uses * ? ~ or starts with < > = (rename it). Red due date: this How Often needs a due date.
Per Paycheck is the average to set aside from each paycheck. The Paychecks tab shows what each paycheck really covers.

Change Pay To: type a different amount for one paycheck (a bonus, overtime, a smaller check). Leave it blank to use your usual paycheck from Start Here.
Plan Balance: your starting balance plus what's left from every paycheck so far. Short means the plan runs out there: save more from the paychecks before it.
Bank Balance does the same with what really happened on Transactions. Each paycheck covers its payday through the day before the next one.
Paid a day early? Date it on your payday so it lands on the right paycheck. Anything before your first payday's month isn't part of the plan.

Filled in automatically from Transactions, by calendar month. Plan So Far = your plan for the months that have transactions.
Pick a goal from your Savings categories (or type your own), then add the Target and what you had saved when you started (Starting Balance).
Added This Year fills in from Transactions: every transfer you log to that category counts.
Per Paycheck comes from Budget Plan. Paychecks to Go = what's left divided by that amount.
Tip: build a starter emergency fund of $1,000 first, then grow it to 3-6 months of expenses.

Pick a debt from your Bills (its payment is a bill on Budget Plan), then type the balance when you started, the interest rate (22.99 or 22.99%) and, once a month, the Current Balance from your statement.
Paid This Year fills in from Transactions. Interest & Charges = what you paid minus how much the balance went down (interest, fees and any new purchases).
Monthly Payment comes from Budget Plan. Months Left assumes you keep paying that amount.
Snowball: pay extra on Payoff Order 1 (the smallest balance) first. When it's gone, roll its payment into the next one.
'Payment too low' means the payment doesn't cover the monthly interest yet. A rate under 1%? Type it with the % sign, like 0.9%.

formula: OR($K2="Payment too low",$K2="Add it to Budget Plan",$K2="Fix a payment")
